Content:
The length of a side of the hexagon [MATH: {S}] is [MATH: 20\, \textrm{in}.] The ratio of the area of the larger hexagon to the area of the smaller one is [MATH: 25:4.] Given that the two hexagons [MATH: {S}] and [MATH: {L}] are similar, what is the length of the side of the hexagon [MATH: {L}?]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/91dcfc654d26bf2713be42badabae589]

Content:
Recall that if two polygons are similar with scale factor [MATH: k,] then the ratio of the two areas is equal to [MATH: k^2.]

Content:
We are told that

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{\mathcal{A}_{L}}{\mathcal{A}_{S}} = \dfrac{25}{4}.]

Content:
So, we have

Content:
[MATH: k^2 = \dfrac{25}{4}\quad\Rightarrow\quad k = \sqrt{\dfrac{25}{4}} = \dfrac{5}{2}.]

Content:
As a result, the side length of polygon [MATH: {L}] is [MATH: \dfrac{5}{2}] times the side length of polygon [MATH: {S}.] Therefore, the side length of the larger polygon is

Content:
[MATH: 20 \cdot \dfrac{5}{2} = 50 \,\textrm{in}.]

[MATH: \dfrac{8}{\left(\dfrac{4}{5}\right)}=10\,\textrm{in} \qquad \textrm{and}\qquad \dfrac{6}{\left(\dfrac{4}{5}\right)}=\dfrac{15}{2}\,\textrm{in}.]
